title: Is Indonesia’s 100 GW Solar Plan Realistic?
author: James Guild
text:
An aerial view of a solar power station in Bali, Indonesia.
Credit: Depositphotos
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has set an extremely ambitious target of building 100 GW of solar capacity by 2029. Naturally, many people are wondering if this a realistic goal. I’ll spare you the suspense. The answer is no. But it does send a strong signal that the government is serious about putting more resources toward cleaner energy.People often look at Indonesia’s energy sector, dominated by coal and other fossil fuels, and the extremely slow progress on renewables to date, and conclude that clean energy is a non-starter. I don’t agree. The government has been signaling for some time that it is willing to pivot toward clean energy. The catch is that it wants to do so on its own terms, without simply opening Indonesia up as a market for private developers and investors where the state-owned utility PLN ends up on the hook for expensive purchase agreements. This, in my estimation, was the major flaw with how Indonesia’s Just Energy Transition Partnership was originally designed.[...]
